data.name: Main_SectionSensors
data.comment: Main window, section heading. Written in upper case in every language.

data.name: Mode_High
data.comment: Performance mode name in the window and the tray menu. Keep close to MSI Center's own label.

data.name: Mode_Balanced
data.comment: Performance mode name in the window and the tray menu. Keep close to MSI Center's own label.

data.name: Mode_Eco
data.comment: Performance mode name in the window and the tray menu: the battery-saving mode. Keep close to MSI Center's own label.

data.name: Common_Apply
data.comment: Button: apply the chosen setting to the laptop.

data.name: Common_Yes
data.comment: Confirmation dialog button.

data.name: Common_No
data.comment: Confirmation dialog button.

data.name: Main_SectionFanProfile
data.comment: Main window, section heading. Written in upper case in every language.

data.name: Main_EditCurves
data.comment: Main window, button that opens the fan curve editor. Keep short.

data.name: Main_EditCurvesTip
data.value: Edit fan curves and custom profiles
data.comment: Tooltip of the Edit curves button.

data.name: Main_SectionPerformance
data.comment: Main window, section heading above the performance modes. Written in upper case in every language.

data.name: Main_PowerSwitch
data.value: Remember separate settings on AC and battery
data.comment: Check box label. AC = plugged in to mains power.

data.name: Main_PowerSwitchTip
data.value: When on, the fan profile and performance mode are remembered separately for AC and battery. Plugging in or unplugging the cable applies the last setting you chose for that source. The charge limit and Cooler Boost do not change.
data.comment: Tooltip of the AC and battery check box.

data.name: Main_CoolerBoostHint
data.comment: Shown next to the Cooler Boost button. Cooler Boost is MSI's name for full-speed fans: keep it untranslated.

data.name: Main_SectionChargeLimit
data.comment: Main window, section heading. Written in upper case in every language.

data.name: Main_ChargeLimitNow
data.comment: Label before the charge limit that is set at the moment, for example Now: 60%.

data.name: Main_Reapply
data.comment: Button next to the warning that the laptop dropped M-Tool's settings (after a restart or sleep).

data.name: Charge_Unknown
data.comment: Charge limit value when it could not be read. Lower case, shown after Now:.

data.name: Charge_Off
data.comment: Charge limit value when the limit is switched off (battery charges to full). Lower case, shown after Now:.

data.name: Format_Percent
data.comment: A percentage, {0} is the number. Follow the way your language writes it: 60%, 60 %, %60.

data.name: Editor_Title
data.comment: Title of the fan curve editor window.

data.name: Editor_SectionProfiles
data.comment: Fan curve editor, section heading. Written in upper case in every language.

data.name: Editor_BuiltIn
data.comment: Tag next to a fan profile that ships with M-Tool. Lower case, short.

data.name: Editor_Copy
data.comment: Button: copy the selected fan profile.

data.name: Editor_Delete
data.comment: Button: delete the selected fan profile.

data.name: Editor_SectionName
data.comment: Fan curve editor, section heading above the profile name box. Written in upper case in every language.

data.name: Editor_Rename
data.comment: Button: rename the selected fan profile.

data.name: Editor_SectionFan
data.comment: Fan curve editor, section heading above the CPU and GPU buttons. Written in upper case in every language.

data.name: Editor_BuiltInReadOnly
data.value: Built-in profiles cannot be changed; copy one to edit it.
data.comment: Shown when a built-in fan profile is selected.

data.name: Editor_ColPoint
data.comment: Column heading: number of the curve point.

data.name: Editor_ColThreshold
data.comment: Column heading: temperature at which the fan speed of this point starts.

data.name: Editor_ColSpeed
data.comment: Column heading: fan speed in percent.

data.name: Editor_ColAllowed
data.comment: Column heading: the range the point may be moved in.

data.name: Editor_AllowedRange
data.comment: Range a curve point may be set to: {0}–{1} temperature, {2}–{3} fan speed in percent.

data.name: Editor_Revert
data.comment: Button: throw away the unsaved changes.

data.name: Editor_Save
data.comment: Button: save the profile.

data.name: Editor_SaveAndApply
data.comment: Button: save the profile and apply it to the laptop.

data.name: Tray_PowerSwitch
data.comment: Tray menu check item. AC = plugged in to mains power.

data.name: Tray_StartAtSignIn
data.comment: Tray menu check item: start M-Tool when the user signs in to Windows.

data.name: Tray_OpenWindow
data.comment: Tray menu item.

data.name: Tray_Exit
data.comment: Tray menu item.

data.name: Tray_Performance
data.comment: Tray menu sub menu title. {0} is the current performance mode name.

data.name: Tray_DataStale
data.comment: Tray tooltip, appended to the profile name when the sensors stopped answering. Keep the leading space and keep it short: the whole tooltip is limited to 127 characters.

data.name: Tray_Paused
data.comment: Tray tooltip, appended to the profile name while sensor reading is paused (sleep). Keep the leading space and keep it short: the whole tooltip is limited to 127 characters.

data.name: Tray_ReadingSensors
data.comment: Tray tooltip line before the first sensor reading. Keep it short: the whole tooltip is limited to 127 characters.

data.name: Startup_Failed
data.comment: Error box. {0} is the reason, {1} the folder of the log files.

data.name: Startup_UnexpectedError
data.comment: Error box. {0} is the reason, {1} the folder of the log files.

data.name: Startup_Problem
data.comment: Error box. {0} is a sentence that says why M-Tool did not open, {1} the folder of the log files.

data.name: Startup_EcUnreachable
data.value:
Could not reach the EC: {0}
Details: {1}
data.comment: Error box. EC = the laptop's embedded controller. {0} is the reason, {1} the folder of the log files.

data.name: Startup_PawnIoMissing
data.comment: SAFETY. Error box. {0} is the install command: copy it unchanged. {1} is the folder of the log files. PawnIO is a product name. EC = the laptop's embedded controller.

data.name: PawnIo_Missing
data.value: PawnIO is not installed. To install: {0}
data.comment: SAFETY. Error text. {0} is the install command: copy it unchanged. PawnIO is a product name.

data.name: Session_FirmwareUnread
data.value: Firmware could not be read at startup. For safety, Cooler Boost and the charge limit are hidden in this session and settings are not written. Restart M-Tool.
data.comment: SAFETY. Warning banner. Firmware = the laptop's embedded controller firmware. Cooler Boost is MSI's name: keep it.

data.name: Probe_UnsupportedWmi2
data.value: This MSI model is not supported yet: it reaches the EC through MSI's WMI2 interface (mostly 11th-generation Intel and later). M-Tool can only read WMI1 models for now. To help add support, run "M-Tool.exe --report --wmi2" in an administrator command prompt and attach the zip it creates to a "Device report" issue on GitHub.
data.comment: SAFETY. Error box. EC = the laptop's embedded controller. Copy the command M-Tool.exe --report --wmi2 unchanged. "Device report" is the name of the GitHub issue type: keep it in English.

data.name: Probe_UnsupportedNoWmi
data.value: This computer is not supported yet: the MSI WMI interface ({0} or {1} in root\WMI) was not found.
data.comment: Error box. {0} and {1} are WMI class names: copy them unchanged.

data.name: Status_FailureTitle
data.value: M-Tool: setting could not be applied
data.comment: Title of the error balloon shown when writing a setting failed. Keep M-Tool.

data.name: Status_ReadOnlyNote
data.value: M-Tool is in monitor-only mode and cannot change settings.
data.comment: SAFETY. Last sentence of the warning banners, passed to them as {2} or {1}. Says the app only monitors and writes nothing.

data.name: Status_DryRun
data.value: Dry-run mode: your choices are checked but not applied to the laptop. To apply them for real, set "dryRun": false in settings.json.
data.comment: SAFETY. Info banner at the top of the window. Copy settings.json and "dryRun": false unchanged: the user types them in the file.

data.name: Status_FirmwareUnread
data.value: The firmware version could not be read. {0}
data.comment: SAFETY. Warning banner. {0} is the sentence 'M-Tool is in monitor-only mode and cannot change settings.' Firmware = the laptop's embedded controller firmware.

data.name: Status_Experimental
data.value: Experimental: this firmware ({0}) is read with the {1} record; the values are not verified on this model and may be wrong. {2}
data.comment: SAFETY. Warning banner. {0} is the firmware version, {1} the name of the device record it is read with (copy it unchanged), {2} the sentence 'M-Tool is in monitor-only mode and cannot change settings.'

data.name: Status_FirmwareFamily
data.value: This firmware ({0}) belongs to the {1} family, but is not verified for changing settings. {2}
data.comment: SAFETY. Warning banner. {0} is the firmware version, {1} the model name (for example MSI P65 Creator 9SE: copy it unchanged), {2} the sentence 'M-Tool is in monitor-only mode and cannot change settings.'

data.name: Status_FirmwareUnsupported
data.comment: SAFETY. Warning banner. {0} is the firmware version, {1} the sentence 'M-Tool is in monitor-only mode and cannot change settings.'

data.name: Status_WritesOff
data.value: Changing settings is off, M-Tool is in monitor-only mode. Reason: {0}
data.comment: SAFETY. Warning banner shown when writing is switched off. {0} is the reason, a sentence.

data.name: Status_Drift
data.value: The laptop's settings differ from your choices ({0}). Press Reapply to restore them.
data.comment: Warning band with a button. {0} is a list of the differing settings, already separated with the list separator of the language. Reapply must match the label of the Reapply button (Main_Reapply).

data.name: Status_DriftFanTable
data.comment: Part of the list in the drift band (Status_Drift). Lower case, no full stop.

data.name: Status_DriftPerformance
data.comment: Part of the list in the drift band (Status_Drift). Lower case, no full stop.

data.name: Status_DriftChargeLimit
data.comment: Part of the list in the drift band (Status_Drift). Lower case, no full stop.

data.name: Status_DriftFanMode
data.comment: Part of the list in the drift band (Status_Drift). Lower case, no full stop.

data.name: Status_FailedRecovered
data.value: {0} For safety, the fans were set back to the factory setting and changing settings was switched off. To switch it on again, run M-Tool.exe --unlock --confirm in an administrator command prompt, then restart M-Tool.
data.comment: SAFETY. Error band and balloon after a failed write that was undone. {0} is the failure sentence. Copy the command M-Tool.exe --unlock --confirm unchanged.

data.name: Status_FailedUnrecovered
data.value: {0} It could not be confirmed that the fans are at a safe setting; as a precaution, an attempt was made to switch Cooler Boost on. Restart the computer; the fans return to the factory setting.
data.comment: SAFETY. Error band and balloon after a failed write that could not be undone. {0} is the failure sentence. Cooler Boost is MSI's name: keep it.

data.name: Controls_FanTableImplausible
data.value: The fan table read from the laptop is not plausible
data.comment: Label of the active fan profile when the table read from the EC holds nonsense values. EC = the laptop's embedded controller.

data.name: Controls_FanProfileUnrecognized
data.comment: Label of the active fan profile when the laptop's fan table matches no profile.

data.name: Controls_PerformanceFactory
data.comment: Performance mode label when the laptop holds a value that is none of the three modes. {0} is the raw value as two hex digits: keep {0:X2} and the 0x.

data.name: Controls_ReadFailed
data.value: The current settings could not be read, the values shown may be old. ({0})
data.comment: Warning band. {0} is the technical reason.

data.name: Controls_NothingToReapply
data.comment: Message after pressing Reapply when no setting is chosen.

data.name: Main_ReapplyStartup
data.value: Settings could not be applied at startup: {0}
data.comment: Warning or error band after the automatic reapply when M-Tool started. {0} is the reason, a sentence.

data.name: Main_ReapplyResume
data.value: Settings could not be applied after waking from sleep: {0}
data.comment: Warning or error band after the automatic reapply when the computer woke from sleep. {0} is the reason, a sentence.

data.name: Main_ReapplyPowerSource
data.value: Settings could not be applied after the power source changed: {0}
data.comment: Warning or error band after the automatic reapply when the computer was plugged in or unplugged. {0} is the reason, a sentence.

data.name: Main_ReapplyRetry
data.value: Settings could not be applied on retry: {0}
data.comment: Warning or error band after the automatic reapply that retries an earlier failure. {0} is the reason, a sentence.

data.name: Sensors_Reading
data.comment: Line under the sensors before the first reading.

data.name: Sensors_Paused
data.comment: Line under the sensors while reading is paused because the computer sleeps.

data.name: Sensors_Stale
data.comment: Line under the sensors when the sensors stopped answering. {0} is the time of the last good reading, already formatted in the language of the window (long time format).

data.name: Sensors_NoData
data.comment: Line under the sensors when the sensors never answered.

data.name: PowerSwitch_OnAc
data.comment: Line under the AC and battery switch. AC = plugged in to mains power.

data.name: PowerSwitch_OnBattery
data.comment: Line under the AC and battery switch.

data.name: SignIn_ForeignTask
data.value: a task M-Tool did not create
data.comment: Part of SignIn_RepairWarning ({0}): the Task Scheduler task with M-Tool's name was not made by M-Tool. Lower case, no full stop.

data.name: SignIn_OtherExe
data.comment: Part of SignIn_RepairWarning ({0}): the task starts another program. {0} is its file path. Lower case, no full stop.

data.name: SignIn_RepairWarning
data.value: Start at sign-in is not the expected task ({0}). To switch it to this exe, turn it off and on again from the tray menu.
data.comment: Warning band. {0} is SignIn_ForeignTask or SignIn_OtherExe. The tray menu item is Tray_StartAtSignIn: use the same wording.

data.name: SignIn_ChangeFailed
data.value: Start at sign-in could not be changed: {0}
data.comment: Warning band. {0} is the technical reason.

data.name: Editor_DiscardQuestion
data.comment: Question in a Yes/No box, asked before leaving a changed fan curve.

data.name: Editor_Saved
data.value: Saved. Press Apply to use it on the fans.
data.comment: Message in the curve editor after saving. Apply must match the label of the Apply button (Common_Apply).

data.name: Editor_SavedNotApplied
data.value: The profile was saved but not applied: another action is running or changing settings is off. Try again in a moment.
data.comment: Message in the curve editor after Save and apply could not apply.

data.name: Editor_DeleteQuestion
data.comment: Question in a Yes/No box. {0} is the profile name, shown in quotes.

data.name: Editor_BusySelect
data.value: Another action is running; you can pick a profile when it is done.
data.comment: Message in the curve editor when a profile is clicked while a command runs.

data.name: List_Separator
data.comment: Between the items of a list written in a sentence, for example the parts in the drift band. Include the space. Use the separator your language writes in prose (for example a comma and a space, or the CJK comma), not the regional list separator.
